newsitem.title: USA: Orange County files must stay sealed-Merrill Lynch.
newsitem.headline: Orange County files must stay sealed-Merrill Lynch.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co has asked an Orange County, Calif., judge to keep county grand jury transcripts sealed to protect proprietary information about the company and safeguard the reputations of its employees, court papers showed Friday.

In a brief filed with Superior Court Judge David Carter, Merrill Lynch's lawyers said the grand jury transcripts contain confidential personal and business information that would "be of great interest and advantage to Merrill Lynch's competitors" if released to the public.

"Information that could be damaging to the reputation of individuals mentioned in testimony would also be revealed to the press in the form of the DA's (district attorney's) working theories of potential criminal liability, including suggestions by the DA, through questioning, that individuals may have been engaged in unlawful or improper conduct," Merrill Lynch said.

Local news organizations and Orange County's own attorneys have asked Judge Carter to grant them access to the grand jury transcripts, which could shed light on Merrill Lynch's role in the county bankruptcy crisis.

The grand jury investigation ended in June when Merrill Lynch agreed to pay $30 million. The controversial settlement ensured that the brokerage gaint and its employees would not face criminal charges.
Lawyers for the county asked Carter earlier this week to give them access to the transcripts for use in the county's $2 billion-plus civil lawsuit against Merrill Lynch.
County prosecutors say the transcripts must remain sealed because no indictments were returned by the grand jury.

"The witnesses who testified revealed confidential information on the understanding that, absent the filing of an indictment, the proceedings would remain secret," Merrill Lynch's lawyers said in their brief. It would be a "profound injustice," they wrote, "if this secrecy is violated."
A court hearing about the transcripts is set for July 30.
